title: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
slides: Can Gemini actually understand what you're really asking?
Google claims sharp gains on complex, multi-part questions
It struggles most when questions contain hidden contradictions
Expect better answers to messy prompts starting this week
Test one tangled question you've asked before
thread_text:
1. Can Gemini Read Between Lines?

Google says its new model makes sharp gains on complex, multi-part questions. But it still struggles when questions contain hidden contradictions.

2. Google's Big Claim

Internal tests show Gemini answers messy, multi-part prompts far better than before. The upgrade starts rolling out this week.

3. Hidden Contradictions Break It

If your prompt contains conflicting assumptions, Gemini still gets confused. That's the one weakness Google admits remains.

4. Better Answers This Week

Starting this week, expect sharper responses to tangled prompts. The improvement targets real-world messy questions, not clean benchmarks.

5. Test Your Worst Prompt

Take one tangled question you've asked before and try it again this week. Does it handle the hidden contradictions? If not, you'll know exactly where it still fails.
